copy.hero_headline: Your dock becomes a station on a connected water network.
copy.hero_sub: Navier is building an employer water network for the DC waterfront — 20-seat electric hydrofoils linking Old Town Alexandria, The Wharf, Georgetown, Navy Yard, and National Harbor, growing to the Pentagon, National Landing (by shuttle), and the Potomac suburbs.
copy.hero_note: Non-binding letter of intent · no commitment · helps us sequence which line launches first · first service no earlier than end-2027
copy.hero_cta_network: Find a route to my office
copy.problem_title: The bridges are the bottleneck. The river is the spare lane.
copy.problem_lead: DC has the worst traffic congestion of any US metro and a river running straight through its densest job clusters. Every launch station is an active water-taxi landing today — no new infrastructure needed on day one.

problem_chips.label: Worst US traffic congestion (2025 metro rank)
Proven Old Town↔Wharf ridership during 2019 Metro shutdown
Your campus plugs into the full network

copy.precedent: When Metro shut down in 2019, a single Old Town↔Wharf boat carried 5,000 riders a day. The launch trigger (60–80 committed seats) is a fraction of that demonstrated flow.
copy.stripe_lesson: We ran the first employer water commute on San Francisco Bay. DC already proved the water works when the bridges fail.
copy.price_anchor: $650–1,200 / seat-month program band — not a DC quote; market-specific pricing TBD
copy.launch_trigger: A line advances when about 60–80 seats are committed on that corridor — enough for real commuter service.
copy.proof_title: DC already proved the water commute.
copy.proof_lead: Active water-taxi landings, a proven ridership spike, and employer campuses on the waterfront.
copy.proof_worked_body: City Cruises runs daily water taxi among Old Town, The Wharf, Georgetown, and National Harbor today.
copy.proof_fixed_body: First employer water commute on SF Bay — ride worked; twenty-seat class is the product.
copy.proof_ask_body: Non-binding LOI — seats or line anchor — so we sequence on real demand.
copy.network_lead: Pick where your people live and where you work. We'll show the water path — including transfers — and compare it to a typical drive. All water times are indicative and subject to DC harbor speed rules.
copy.network_footnote: Gold rings mark transfer hubs (Old Town Alexandria primary; The Wharf). Stops are usable marina/pier berths. National Landing connects by ground shuttle from Daingerfield Island — no dock at HQ2. Georgetown and Navy Yard legs run under no-wake / 6 mph regimes — no bare crossing-time claims.
copy.map_detail_empty: Pick two terminals in Find my ride — or select a line or stop.
copy.calc_lead_html: Optional planning math. Seat pricing uses the global program band ($650–1,200), not a DC quote. If you ran Find my ride, times can be prefilled from that route.
copy.loi_cta: Non-binding. Helps us sequence Potomac lines to real demand at your terminal.
copy.footer_note: Letters of intent are non-binding. Service launch not before end-2027. Map is coverage narrative, not a service promise.
copy.office_lead: You don't need a stop on every line. Sit on a hub — or any stop that feeds one — and riders transfer to you. Tap a campus to set it as your office and see who can reach you at launch vs full network.
copy.office_insight: Example: an LOI at The Wharf still serves Old Town, National Harbor, and Georgetown riders on day one — and Pentagon / National Landing (shuttle) riders as the network grows.
copy.why_lead: The bridges are the bottleneck. The Potomac is the spare lane — terminal to terminal, above the traffic.
